reachable: Yes — verified by execution, not by reading. This is an objective-axis impl, so it can only touch the scored read through the weights it trains, which is exactly what it claims. I loaded the real training root (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, 2560 trajectories), applied M.standardize_stats/apply_stats the way cloud/build_context.py:149-150 does, drew a batch with the genome's OWN batcher (r6_sysblock_hardneg_curriculum, bs=64 from evolve/genome.py:24 default) through baseline_interleave.collate, and reconstructed pred/tgt/ctx["cmd"] exactly as evolve/harness.py:91-99 does (n=1916 rows, matching the hypothesis's n=1920). On that batch the routed mechanism is live: `moved` is ~1.0 on 348 rows (18.2%), including ALL 64 cups_test rows and ALL 64 cups_expose rows — the compositional slice the metric scores. Gradient reaches pred on all 1916 rows; grad into ctx["cmd"] is None (detached as claimed); the loss is finite and anti-collapse-safe (constant prediction 6.039 vs perfect prediction 0.403). Squared-gradient mass on routed rows moves from 19.3% under plain MSE to 82.6% under this objective, and on blank-observation rows from 35.6% to 4.8% — the direction and rough magnitude of the reallocation claim, measured on real data rather than the author's synthetic. Substituting the name-decoy content into all 64 cups_test rows of a perfect prediction costs +1.120 under this objective vs +0.0479 under MSE, a 23.4x ratio (the hypothesis claims 44x, explicitly on synthetic data). Speed: 3 forward+backward at n=1916 on CPU = 0.170 s (claimed 0.12 s). No regime problem: the mechanism does not depend on the "command present, observation absent" condition that is identically false in training, and it does not read anything the collate does not provide.
summary: The code implements the hypothesis. Every formula in section 2 matches the source line for line: eps_dup = 0.005*2*mean(tgt^2) (:71), group<=4 (:98), moved = has_partner * clamp((1-min_j cos)/0.02,0,1) (:110-113), the +/-32 band (:102), a = (1+kappa*n_neg*softmax(cos/tau))/(1+kappa) added as log(a) with kappa=4 tau=0.05 (:120-122), the hinge softplus((d_true+0.5-d_decoy)/0.25) against the single argmax-cosine in-band candidate (:126,:135-137), and total = mse + 0.5*mse_routed + 1.0*listwise + 0.2*hinge (:148). All masks/weights are detached and only pred carries gradient (verified: ctx["cmd"].grad is None). The three DATA claims it is built on are real and I reproduced them: the jail-sample group-size histogram and the 95/724 = 13.1% role table come back verbatim; the routed read's target is bit-identical to its expose's; and fact (d), the name decoy, is confirmed on the real root — the argmax-cosine negative of `cat /tmp/w/cups/etc/cron.d/backup.job.6` is `cat /tmp/w/cups/etc/cron.d/backup.job`, the WRONG content's expose, in 39 of 53 same-trajectory cases. The divergences are all descriptive/quantitative, none change the mechanism: (1) "negatives only from the same trajectory / the same board" is 45% same-trajectory in practice, because the band is on flattened row index and trajectories are 26-32 rows; (2) the routed set is 18.2% of rows, not 13%, because the code flags both members of a duplicate pair (so the mse_routed multiplier is 3.7x, not 4.8x, and expose rows are upweighted alongside test rows); (3) "the closest genuinely-distinct pair is orders of magnitude further" is false (256-token encoder truncation puts 21,802 distinct-string pairs at distance ~0), but the group<=4 gate absorbs it — small-group partner pairs are 406/416 = 97.6% string-identical; (4) the author's own failure analysis understates the group-size window (320 rows, not 65), which favours the candidate. Two claims I could NOT check: the synthetic-batch figures in section 3 (72%/6.7% gradient mass, 44x decoy penalty) are unreproducible without the author's synthetic construction, but they are explicitly labelled synthetic and the real-data direction holds with smaller magnitudes (82.6%/19.3%, 23.4x); and I cannot say whether the objective actually moves comp_ca, which the author correctly declines to predict.

divergences.claim: "The listwise softmax for anchor i draws its negatives only from rows within +/-32 positions in the flattened order -- the same trajectory, i.e. the other CONTENTS ON THE SAME BOARD" (hypothesis.txt:72-74), and "The eval's forced-foil candidate set IS the set of contents exposed on this board, so the band makes the training discrimination the same discrimination the metric scores." (hypothesis.txt:78-80)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The band is on the FLATTENED row index, not on trajectory identity. Real trajectories in the training root are 26-32 steps (mean 29.6), so a +/-32 band around a row spans 65 rows of which at most 32 belong to the anchor's own trajectory; the rest are the adjacent trajectories, i.e. different boards (usually the same image, because r6_sysblock_hardneg_curriculum concentrates 6-8 images per batch). Measured on a real batch: 45.0% of the 49,910 in-band negative pairs are same-trajectory, 55% are not. The mechanism is still a large concentration versus the parent (whole-batch negatives over n=1916 would be ~1.6% same-trajectory), and the negative that actually dominates the term — the near-one-hot decoy at tau=0.05 — is same-trajectory for 39 of 53 cups_test anchors (74%). Nothing is corrupted (off-board negatives are genuinely different contents, so they are not false negatives), but "only ... the same trajectory / the same board" is wrong for the majority of the negative set.

divergences.claim: "Rows in small groups that duplicate an earlier row: 95 of 724 = 13.1% ... That is the compositional slice" (hypothesis.txt:31-33); "only ~13% to the routed reads" (:112); "mse_routed ... weight 0.5, which on a 13%-routed batch multiplies the regression pressure on the routed reads by ~4.8x" (:68-70).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The 13.1% figure counts only the LATER member of each duplicate pair. The code has no notion of "earlier": `partner` is symmetric, so both members of a routed pair are flagged. On a real batch, moved is essentially binary (348 rows at ~1.0, 23 at <=3.3e-5 numerical noise, 1568 at 0), i.e. 18.2% of rows, not 13%. The mse_routed multiplier is therefore 1 + 0.5/0.182 = 3.7x, not ~4.8x. The upweighted set also includes the EXPOSE rows (cups_expose 64, cvar_expose 101), which are first-sight reads, not routed recalls — the description names the mechanism "ROUTED-RECALL DETECTION" and says it selects rows "whose target is an exact duplicate of another row's target ... AND whose command ... is not the same command as its duplicate partner's, so the content reached this row by an intervening command" (module DESCRIPTION, lines 10-13), which is true of the expose row only in the reverse temporal direction.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/objective/r2_routed_recall_namedecoy.py:110-113 (symmetric `partner`, `moved` written for every anchor). Executed: `moved>0: 371 0.193632572889328`; `count moved>0.5: 348 count 0<moved<=0.5: 23`; roles `[('cvar_test',108),('cvar_expose',101),('cups_expose',64),('cups_test',64),('read',13),('cwd_anchor',12),('cups_ctx',9)]`. The 724-step jail-sample statistics themselves reproduce EXACTLY (group-size histogram, 95/724 = 13.1%, role table cvar_test 51 / cups_test 24 / cwd_anchor 8 / cvar_expose 5 / cups_ctx 4 / read 3).

divergences.claim: "bit-equal targets sit at ~1e-7, the closest genuinely-distinct pair is orders of magnitude further" (hypothesis.txt:60-61).
divergences.what_the_code_does: False as stated: the frozen encoder truncates at max_length=256 tokens (realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:68), so observations with different render_obs strings that share a 256-token prefix produce IDENTICAL embeddings at distance 0.0. In the real batch, 21,802 of 82,506 pairs below eps_dup have different render_obs strings. The design is saved by the group<=4 gate, which the hypothesis introduces for a different reason: all of those collisions live in the blank / cvar_op mega-groups. Among small-group partner pairs — the ones that actually feed `moved` — only 10 of 416 (2.4%) have differing strings. Bit-equal pairs measured at <=2.9e-6, not ~1e-7, still two orders below eps_dup = 0.0101.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/objective/r2_routed_recall_namedecoy.py:71, :96-98. Executed: `eps_dup 0.010079953819513321`; `mean offdiag tt 2.0162`; `equal-string pair dist: max 2.86e-06`; `distinct-string pair dist: min 0.0`; `dup pairs with EQUAL obs string: 60704  with DIFFERENT obs string: 21802`; `small-group partner pairs: same-string 406 different-string 10`.

divergences.claim: "the gate is computed inside a +/-32 band, not globally. If a batch region happened to contain fewer than five blank observations in a 65-row window, a blank pair with two different commands would be flagged as routed" (hypothesis.txt:136-138).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The group-size count is not over the 65-row band — `grp_c = dup_cc.sum(dim=1)` counts over the entire chunk candidate window, up to 256+32+32 = 320 rows. The stated failure mode is therefore even less reachable than the author believed. Measured: blank-observation rows have group sizes 45-113 (median 108) and 0 of 794 blank rows fall at group<=4. This divergence is in the author's own failure analysis and runs in the candidate's favour.
